descriptions.previous_title: Bind Petal reviews to selected accounts and actual EVM/Solana signing bytes
descriptions.previous_body:
Machine now forwards the full transaction/message envelopes needed for Broker-owned clear signing and binds preparation/retry to the selected account and actual signing bytes. App-written descriptions cannot replace the Broker's reading.

- Forward supported login/payment/exchange reviews and Hyperliquid use-time witnesses; preserve exact account selection and conservative retry/downgrade behavior. Polymarket uses the one-signature `polymarket.clob_auth.v1` profile.
- Preserve existing raw Pump forwarding and blockhash-independent durable identity without changing the guest ABI. Pump.fun is excluded from the user's remaining acceptance target.
- Pin Broker `b10cc950405261ba43e7e953e292507db97a47f7` in all six API/lock/release/CI files. Its Enso catalog covers the twelve networks actually accepted by the Petal, including HyperEVM, Linea, Tempo and Robinhood. Pair with [Enso #16](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-petal-enso/pull/16), which binds same-chain receiver/output checks and preserves the reviewed calldata floor during refresh.
- Retain a pinned wider route inventory with explicit limits and the narrowed acceptance scope: the five default-enabled Petals are **Enso, Hyperliquid, Polymarket, NEAR Intents and Feedback**. Earlier work on other Petals is preserved, not a gate for these five.

Current local verification: exact-pin affected Machine library suite **297 passed/one existing ignored**, strict affected all-target Clippy and format. Broker's exact pinned workspace passed **507 tests/one ignored**; [hosted CI](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/actions/runs/39271329417) passed, including privileged W0. Enso's Petal suite passed 140 tests, 31 route components and package validation; six private-EVM pinned-contract cases proved output checks and atomic rollback. [Pinned Enso review evidence](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/blob/3e970902b892ad4204db8758de15bf75f8a2c18b/tests/evidence/enso-route-review-2026-10-19.json) records eight actual Petal-preparation→Broker-reading roundtrips and sixteen desktop/mobile views, including native artwork. These fixtures do not establish API discovery, funded venue or physical-owner acceptance.

[Machine CI](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271571840) and [validator](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271571775) passed. Both Linux release targets passed; the macOS job in the [release dry run](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271589674) and [macOS Unix conformance](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271598087) are still running. They use Machine `3e970902b892ad4204db8758de15bf75f8a2c18b`, Broker above and compatibility Signer `bc88ad690757165ebf1978410ea5c7ec652215d3`. Signer #66 is a separate preserved dependency. Earlier green runs describe earlier combinations. Two-login macOS lacks runner/login identities; production signing/publication is excluded.

The pin helper intentionally flags schema-1 migration dev fixtures (Broker `dd2add2b9d41540521d08c77d19fb467a2d8029e`/runtime `5db670e1b7507deabfdcf451be8b5d315c1c9d91`), excluded from production normal/build graphs. The new Broker commit is unlanded. Fresh reviews, specific merge approvals, landed repins, final owner/venue acceptance and matching package/catalog/service publication remain in [PM #80](https://github.com/bloom-directory/pm/issues/80). Nested shortcut effects and unknown identities remain explicit. No merge or production release is authorized.

- [x] Behavior tests cover omitted reviews, account binding, tampering, retry and downgrade/failure cases.
- [x] Architecture documented in `docs/architecture/Sealed Approvals.md`.
- [x] Sealed Approval invariants preserved; review grants no additional custody/submission authority.
- [x] Agent guidance documents supported review binding, retry and unknown-state limits; no guest ABI change.

## Review reconciliation (2026-10-19)

- Keep Polymarket orders exact. The reusable Trader proposal in #352 must use exact approval or remain unavailable until a separately reviewed, versioned trading profile exists. The client now reports the exact-approval requirement for all reviewed message classes, rather than a misleading Polymarket-only error. All 69 client library tests, affected all-target strict Clippy and format pass.
- Document the removed `reviewMode` field and its migration, package/catalog compatibility requirements, evidence references, and the token-policy integration rule in `docs/architecture/Sealed Approvals.md`. These are decisions and integration requirements, not claims that #322/#293/#352 have been changed.
- Catalog publication remains blocking: compatible caller releases, full catalog/lineage/authority-route updates, and existing-wallet package approval are required. Do not ship the old catalog with this Machine.
- Pump already requires one operation and one signature in the pinned Broker. Broker [2b7033a](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/commit/2b7033a) adds a passing real Unix Broker→Signer regression: after signing and reopening Broker, a second blockhash is refused with `LimitExceededOperations`. This proves single-use authority for the fixture; it is not a funded Pump trade.
- Broker must land before final production repins. The existing compatibility Signer is landed `bc88ad690757165ebf1978410ea5c7ec652215d3`; Signer #66 is separate, not the current runtime pin.
- The earlier all-platform release dry run 39271589674 passed; it covers `3e970902`, not this follow-up. Two-login macOS, physical-owner/venue acceptance, fresh independent review and explicit merge approvals remain outstanding.

descriptions.previous_title: Decode EVM and Solana transactions, payments and exchange signatures
descriptions.previous_body:
Owners previously saw hash-only signing payloads and incomplete protocol/token facts. Broker now reconstructs supported signing bytes, binds the review to the approval and displays actual accounts, assets, amounts, counterparties, permissions and limits.

- Compile exact-network/address EVM and Safe readers with token units/artwork. Read ERC-20, ERC-4626/Bundler, Safe creation/signatures/execution/batches/deployments and native Privacy Pools shapes; preserve raw unsupported content with a reason.
- Rebuild bounded EIP-712/EIP-191/SIWE, ordered Hyperliquid actions, Polymarket ERC-7739 orders and DepositWallet batches. Known classes require complete envelopes and selected-account/bound checks. Hyperliquid delegated use-time witnesses are reconstructed before authority reservation, without another ceremony per trade. Immutable `polymarket.clob_auth.v1` permits one selected-owner authentication signature with guarded freshness; older reusable onboarding grants are refused.
- Read Enso Router V2 fungible inputs and safe-route receiver/output balance-increase checks on **all twelve networks accepted by the enabled Enso Petal**, including HyperEVM, Linea, Tempo and Robinhood. Output units come from their own bytes and exact token identity; outputs cannot authorize native input value. Empty checks warn. Pair with [Enso #16](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-petal-enso/pull/16), which prepares the executable output checks and preserves their reviewed floor through refresh.
- Preserve previously implemented independent legacy/v0 Pump readings and one-operation binding of every byte except recent blockhash. Unknown lookup/mint/program/effect facts remain explicit. Native Solana proof-verifier sources/digest and SDK ABI are unchanged. **Pump.fun is outside the user's remaining acceptance scope**, not a release gate for the enabled Petals.

The current product acceptance target is Bloom's five default-enabled Petals: Enso, Hyperliquid, Polymarket, NEAR Intents and Feedback. Wider implementation history stays in this PR; it does not expand that target. [PM #80](https://github.com/bloom-directory/pm/issues/80) is the single tracker.

Validation at current Broker `b10cc950405261ba43e7e953e292507db97a47f7`: full workspace **507 passed/one existing ignored** and strict all-target workspace Clippy/format; [hosted CI](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/actions/runs/39271329417) passed, including privileged W0. Nine authenticated Unix Broker↔Signer custody tests include store-reopen proofs of Pump byte binding and Hyperliquid delegated preimage verification/signatures. These are software-owner fixtures, not physical-passkey or venue-effect acceptance. Enso tests cover all twelve exact deployments and refusal of wrong targets/networks. Eight actual Petal-preparation→Broker-reading roundtrips pass, with sixteen desktop/mobile views and ten protocol regressions. Native amount cards use explicit reader annotations; ETH has its own artwork, and zero-value Tempo calls require no invented native currency. Linea/Robinhood ETH units are included.

Matching Machine [#224](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/pull/224) pins this exact Broker commit in production API/lock/release/CI inputs; compatibility Signer is `bc88ad690757165ebf1978410ea5c7ec652215d3`. [All-platform release dry run](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271589674) and [macOS Unix conformance](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/actions/runs/39271598087) are **running**, not yet passed. Earlier green runs apply to older catalog revisions. Production publication is excluded; two-login macOS still lacks runner/login identities.

Nested shortcut/runtime/intermediate effects, arbitrary unknown asset/market identities and cross-chain destination settlement remain unverified. Enso output checks constrain successful execution; they do not prove received funds. Publish matching enabled caller packages and services together. Fresh independent reviews, specific approval for each merge, landed repins and final-set owner/venue acceptance remain. No merge, funded transaction or production release is authorized.


## Pump single-use regression

The `pump_review_binds_real_signer_to_the_reviewed_transaction` test now signs once, reopens Broker, changes only the blockhash and attempts a second operation under the same approval. The actual Unix Broker→Signer fixture refuses it with `LimitExceededOperations`. The focused test, format and diff checks pass. This is test-only: production code remains identical to Machine #224's pinned `b10cc950405261ba43e7e953e292507db97a47f7`. The existing one-operation/one-signature limit resolves the duplicate-signing concern; no funded execution is claimed.

descriptions.previous_title: Enforce Enso receiver and minimum output in signed calldata
descriptions.previous_body:
Enso routes need an executable same-chain output floor and destination tracking that distinguishes bridge delivery from the keeper transaction that performs the swap. This change prepares safe Router V2 calls locally, preserving the router, inputs, native value and inner bytes. Conflicting output token, receiver or minimum constraints are refused; quote refresh preserves the stronger reviewed calldata floor. Cross-chain refresh preserves the exact reviewed shortcut and requires a new intent if it changes.

Settlement tracks LayerZero, CCIP, Relay, Arbitrum Native and CCTP through fixed API paths with a ten-second cache. Intent execution, delivery, manual recovery and refunds stay distinct. Destination completion requires a matching successful receipt on the requested network and enough net incoming token logs; direct native transfers additionally require an undelegated EOA at the same canonical block. Multi-hop completion requires contiguous delivered chain/hash links. Linkage is labelled `provider_asserted`; internal native transfers without trace evidence remain unverified. Polling retains all evidence and returns a retry hint.

Validation: 146 route tests, strict Clippy/format, architecture check, 31 compiled components, Petal check/package. Twelve private-EVM cases passed against pinned Enso Router V2/Weiroll/OpenZeppelin sources: six Router execution/rollback cases and six Rust-decoder versus Solidity-encoder differentials. Unsigned desktop/mobile reviews passed. These are fixture checks, not funded API-route or physical-owner acceptance.

Dependencies: destination receipt/transaction reads and canonical-block code reads require the prepared Machine branch [enso-destination-receipt-reads](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/tree/905fef29b8557db2ba135c5143119aa3180df75a). Nested command readings require the prepared Broker branch [enso-shortcut-command-reader](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/tree/51cb3b614e0317567b68f316e5ba9f494fa2701a). Another session now owns their integration into Bloom #224 and Broker #103; these additions are not yet those PR heads.

[Current Petal CI](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-petal-enso/actions/runs/39281845359) is queued. Earlier green CI covers the earlier output-check implementation. No merge, funded transaction, physical ceremony or production publication was performed.

descriptions.previous_title: Review Hyperliquid typed signatures and complete exchange actions
descriptions.previous_body:
Hyperliquid approval requests previously carried only a preimage/hash, hiding the typed message or ordered exchange action. This change supplies the full action, network, nonce, vault and expiry alongside owner-signature requests. User-signed operations carry complete typed data. [Broker #103](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/pull/103) rebuilds the commitment through [Machine #224](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/pull/224).

Delegated agent actions also send that full public witness through the existing `claim_assurance_evidence` channel at every signing use. Broker reconstructs the actual preimage before authority reservation/signing under the existing grant. No per-trade owner ceremony is added. Existing payload bytes, hashes, custody, retry identities and scope are preserved; old hash-only agent callers require this coordinated package upgrade.

Unknown market IDs keep their exact identity without invented tickers/artwork. Venue agent authorization has no spending ceiling/duration: Petal session caps are local controls. Action/preimage verification does not prove caps, market identity, fills or settlement, and assurance remains MachineAsserted.

SDK/builder/CI/release tooling is pinned to landed Petal `2beed2ff344ce2b0c112e07096027e1ae0404007`. Publish matching packages/catalog/services together.

Validation at 2390d3ad: 55 route tests, strict all-target Clippy, formatting, architecture guard, 74 components and canonical capability/package checks pass. Existing official SDK vectors remain unchanged. Broker's 21 message tests include altered action/network/nonce/vault/expiry, missing or wrong-suite witnesses, non-L1 misuse and a large cancellation batch; full Broker workspace 489 pass/one ignored. Canonical candidate package `0b078996ccc2075747602642302b4db7cb29f212bbc528dcd221f8ea87aefcdc`, archive SHA256 `a73c7424405394c96c166f722a3e9bc1e94500b8278203382c1e6f21a435cf6c`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-petal-hyperliquid/actions/runs/39181190882) passed.

[Historical real-service proof](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/blob/7d66a829f41f6a38bf3ba5f2b07448244dea697d/tests/evidence/hyperliquid-review-candidate-2026-10-18.json) prepared USDC send, owner order and leverage reviews through actual isolated services; all were inspected and cancelled before exchange signing/submission. Its exact older revisions and installed digest remain in that proof. It does not establish the new delegated-use path, a venue order, fill, funded withdrawal or final owner acceptance.

Part of [PM #80](https://github.com/bloom-directory/pm/issues/80). Ready for independent review; specific merge approval and coordinated publication remain required.

descriptions.previous_title: Bind CLOB login to a versioned, one-use authentication permission
descriptions.previous_body:
CLOB authentication and deposit-wallet permissions previously shared `polymarket.onboard`, even though authentication refreshes its server timestamp after owner approval. Give authentication the distinct `polymarket.clob_auth.v1` permission so Broker can verify the actual future message without allowing that grant to sign orders or wallet calls.

The matching [Broker #103](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom-broker/pull/103) enforces one operation/signature, Polygon ClobAuthDomain version 1, selected owner, nonce zero, the fixed wallet attestation and a timestamp within 300 seconds of its guarded clock at signing. A wider profile requires a new class. [Machine #224](https://github.com/bloom-directory/bloom/pull/224) forwards exact order/wallet-batch review records separately. Existing old login hints differ and are replaced; exact permissions keep their own class.

Validation: 94 route tests, strict all-target Clippy, all 109 route component builds, capability checks and deterministic packaging pass. Package digest: `c0c0f646d3e47de77ecd599a6bae0273c05ca2be0725a2129b98d15e25cae474`. Broker reconstruction tests cover wrong owner/domain/nonce/attestation, stale/future timestamps, excess signatures and limits, and old reusable-grant refusal. This does not establish physical-passkey acceptance, live credential creation or funded trading/settlement.

Publish with the matching Broker/Machine services. Older services cannot enforce this profile. API credentials confer account API access and remain secret; this is not a promise of harmless read-only authentication. No new SDK ABI, production publication or merge is included. Tracked in [PM #80](https://github.com/bloom-directory/pm/issues/80).
